subject: Dawn Differential: negotiating tri-region deep-dive slots
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@asteria.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dawn Differential: negotiating tri-region deep-dive slots

Alex —

Thanks again for the quick sync last week. Were excited to run the technical deep-dive with your architects (hands-on run of the model, latency/cost knobs, KV-cache demo and rollout pattern). Before we lock time, a couple of constraints weve seen come up across tri-region teams: DST differences (US/EU), SGT/JST fixed offsets, and hand-off windows for engineers.

To keep this concrete, weve prepared a short candidate list that tries to balance: (a) a meaningful contiguous overlap for a 90-minute session, (b) not forcing anyone past 20:00 local, and (c) an option that anchors on UTC for predictable calendar behavior. Can you ask the team to pick preferred slots (1-4) or suggest alternates? I attached a simple matrix (timezone_matrix.xlsx) and an .ics with all candidates.

Candidate slots (UTC / SF / London / Singapore):
- Slot 1 — 13:00UTC (06:00 PDT / 14:00 BST / 21:00 SGT) — good for EU+APAC evening, early SF (tough for SF folks)
- Slot 2 — 15:00UTC (08:00 PDT / 16:00 BST / 23:00 SGT) — pushes SGT late (acceptable if under 60-90m)
- Slot 3 — 00:00 UTC next day (17:00 PDT / 01:00 BST next day? wait)

Apologies, small mistake above: updated candidates are in the attached file with local times per attendee. My ask:
- Please reply with 1/2/3/4 preference or propose a 90-min contiguous window that works for the architects.
- If you prefer two focused 60-min sessions (engineering + ops), indicate that too.

Well coordinate with Karthik on the lab plan (we need ~45 continuous mins for live model runs + 15min warmup).

Thanks — 
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: timezone_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)] [Attachment: proposed_slots.ics (calendar)]

From: Alex Nguyen <alex@asteria.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Cho <emma.cho@asteria.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 17:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Dawn Differential: negotiating tri-region deep-dive slots

Vanessa, thanks for the clear options. Quick context on our side so your slot matrix maps well:
- Our architecture team is split: London (BST), Singapore (SGT), and a single lead in SF (PDT).
- UK is currently on BST (UTC+1), Singapore is UTC+8 (no DST), SF is on PDT (UTC-7).
- Wed like to avoid anything that starts for the SGT team after 21:00 local if possible.

Preferences:
- We prefer a single 90-minute session if youre able to keep the hands-on portion to ~45 minutes (we can take some async pre-reads).
- Candidate slots 1/2 as you listed are close; slot 2 pushes SGT late.

Availability this week (local blocks):
- London: 13:00-17:30 BST (12:00-16:30 UTC)
- Singapore: 09:00-18:00 SGT (01:00-10:00 UTC)
- SF: 07:30-11:30 PDT (14:30-18:30 UTC) — SF is the biggest constraint

If you can propose a slot that hits ~15:00 UTC, thats a reasonable compromise for all three regions (SF early, London mid-afternoon, Singapore late evening but within 21:00). Otherwise, were open to a split into two 60-min blocks (first for architecture/requirements, second for hands-on).

Ill check with Emma (she schedules the architects) and shell confirm preferred numbers.

— Alex
Lead Systems Architect | Asteria Systems

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@asteria.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dawn Differential: negotiating tri-region deep-dive slots

Thanks Alex — I made a tighter set of four concrete options (times below are local for each region; see attached XLSX for conversion and an .ics you can import):

Option A (best for EU anchor)
- 15:00 UTC / 08:00 PDT / 16:00 BST / 23:00 SGT — 90 minutes

Option B (UTC anchor, earlier APAC)
- 13:00 UTC / 06:00 PDT / 14:00 BST / 21:00 SGT — 90 minutes

Option C (split cadence, two sessions)
- Day 1: 14:00 UTC (60 min) — architecture + rollout
- Day 2: 01:00 UTC (60 min) — hands-on lab (this is 18:00 PDT / 02:00 BST / 09:00 SGT next day)

Option D (rotation-friendly)
- 15:00 UTC on Day 1 (90min) with repeating series that rotates calendar anchor for fairness across teams

Technical note: Karthik flagged that for a smooth hands-on run well want ~15min at the start for model warmups, and a contiguous 45-minute window for the live KV/cache demo. If we split into two sessions we can reduce late-night burden for SGT.

Action: please reply with preference (A/B/C/D) and well send a firm invite. If you prefer we can use a shorter lab (30m) and go heavy on walkthroughs instead.

Attachments: proposed_slots.ics, deepdive-agenda.md, timezone_matrix.xlsx

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 07:14:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Dawn Differential: negotiating tri-region deep-dive slots

Quick engineering constraints to help pick: 
- Live model runs need a contiguous 40-50 minute window to reproduce perf characteristics (warmup + run). Recommend we budget 60 minutes for the lab block to include a 10-15 minute buffer for KV cache warmup.
- Network tracing and token-level cost breakdowns add ~10 minutes; we can run those in parallel but its cleaner to keep them in the same contiguous block.
- If we do the split (Option C), schedule the hands-on lab during the session that lines up with APAC morning (09:00 SGT) on Day 2 so engineers in Singapore can lead the run and SF can observe earlier in their day.

Fallback policy: if we cant find a same-day 90-min overlap, I recommend two 60-min sessions staggered by 12 hours to keep everyone below 21:00 local. Also recommend we record the hands-on portion and capture the KV cache artifacts to replay for anyone who misses the live window.

Ill prepare the lab checklist and upload to the Drive link Vanessa shared.

— Karthik
Staff Engineer, Performance | Redwood Inference
